<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Task Type | Bug fix — verification policy preflight and init preservation |

### What Was Claimed

A schema-valid required `npm test` policy can target a repository root without a test script in a monorepo, so orchestration reaches implementation before discovering that the immutable approved command cannot run. ForgeDock must support safe package working directories, statically reject impossible required checks before writers, and keep genuinely configured required checks fail-closed.

### What We Found

- The frozen base already contains a repository-relative `cwd` field, path canonicalization, and static preflight coverage for missing directories, executables, and npm-family scripts.
- Work-on calls preflight after creating the isolated base worktree but before `materializeForgeAgents`, journal launch, or any writer spawn, which is the correct trust boundary for checking the frozen base.
- `/forge:init` parses an existing policy but unconditionally writes `verification.commands: {}`. Re-running setup therefore silently removes all tracked local checks, including valid monorepo commands and required checks that should remain fail-closed.
- New template setup starts with an empty command map, but the UI does not state that this is an intentional CI-only choice or offer a safe way to retain/validate existing local commands.
- The existing script recognizer handles direct `npm|pnpm|yarn|bun` test/run forms but diagnostics can be made more actionable by naming `/forge:init` and the exact policy path.

### Root Cause

Policy initialization treats verification commands as transient setup output instead of a tracked safety contract. Although the runtime preflight now validates the selected `cwd`, initialization discards the contract before the next run. This can disable required local verification without operator intent and makes setup behavior ambiguous for monorepos.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ui/commands.ts` | Preserve validated tracked commands and make CI-only setup explicit. |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Keep static package checks and improve remediation diagnostics. |
| `src/core/policy.ts` | Existing `cwd` normalization is the policy contract to preserve. |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Existing preflight placement is the writer gate to regression-test. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Extend monorepo and remediation coverage. |
| `test/ui/commands.test.ts` | Cover init verification-policy selection/preservation through pure setup behavior. |

### Evidence

- `.forge/config.json` currently has a required `check` command bound to `cwd: "."`; the code path reads it, then `/forge:init` replaces the command map with `{}`.
- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` resolves and realpaths `cwd`, rejects escapes/control directories, checks executable availability, and reads only `package.json` scripts.
- The monorepo fixture has no root `test` script and a `web/package.json` `test` script; root selection fails and `web` selection passes.
- `startIssue` invokes preflight before `materializeForgeAgents` and before either direct or orchestrated writer launch.
- `child-runtime.ts` independently resolves the bound `cwd` before executing an approved check and preserves nonzero exit status, retaining fail-closed post-implementation behavior.

### History Findings

No additional mutable history was accepted as authority beyond the frozen base. The frozen source and tests show that cwd/preflight work was already introduced, while init command preservation and explicit CI-only signaling remain incomplete.

### Recommendation

Keep the existing static preflight and safe cwd contract. Change setup to retain an existing tracked command map (after static validation), leave a new template explicitly CI-only, surface the mode in setup output, and strengthen diagnostics/tests without executing repository commands during preflight.

### Related Issues

- Issue #94 — required verification policy is not preflighted for monorepos.

### Decomposition Assessment

Single bounded change across policy setup, static preflight diagnostics, and regression tests. No decomposition or product decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Approved commands have a validated repository-relative working directory.
- [ ] `/forge:init` never invents `npm test` for a package without a matching script; new setup remains explicitly CI-only and existing commands are retained rather than silently removed.
- [ ] Required commands are statically preflighted against the frozen worktree before any writer launches.
- [ ] Missing executable, package directory, or npm script errors include the exact policy path and a concrete `/forge:init`/config remediation.
- [ ] Monorepo regression coverage distinguishes root-without-script from a valid package cwd.
- [ ] Required checks that fail after implementation remain blocking.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Make required verification policy safe for monorepos before writers launch, preserve existing tracked local checks during `/forge:init`, and make CI-only setup explicit without executing repository code during preflight.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/ui/commands.ts` — retain normalized tracked verification commands and report local/CI-only setup mode.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` — improve static failure remediation while preserving path and script safety checks.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` — regression coverage for monorepo package selection and actionable failures.
- `test/ui/commands.test.ts` — pure setup-policy preservation/CI-only summary coverage.
- `README.md` — document that `/forge:init` preserves configured local checks and that an empty map is intentional CI-only verification, if needed.

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not execute npm, package scripts, hooks, or arbitrary repository code during preflight.
- Do not permit absolute paths, traversal, symlink escapes, Git/Forge control directories, or unapproved command names.
- Do not weaken required-check fail-closed behavior after implementation.
- Do not change branch, lease, GitHub auth, PR, merge, close, review, or protected-branch authority.
- Do not add domain-specific bypasses or silently remove tracked required checks.

### Invariants

- Every required command resolves a canonical repository-relative directory before writer launch.
- Missing executable, package directory, malformed package manifest, or missing npm-family script fails with the exact policy path and remediation.
- Existing parsed command definitions, including `cwd`, `argv`, `required`, and timeout, remain tracked when setup is rerun.
- A new template with no commands remains an explicit CI-only policy and never invents `npm test`.
- Post-implementation `forge_verify` status handling remains unchanged and required nonzero checks block merge.
- All changes remain within the assigned worktree and use one writer.

### Deliverables

- Preserve verification commands in the policy assembled by `/forge:init` instead of replacing them with `{}`.
- Surface whether setup retained local commands or selected CI-only verification.
- Include concrete `/forge:init` or config remediation in static preflight errors.
- Add/extend regression tests for root-without-script versus `web` package, missing directory/script/executable diagnostics, and command preservation semantics.
- Keep documentation aligned with the tracked policy behavior.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Working-directory field is safe and validated | Reuse existing `normalizeVerificationCommandCwd` and `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory`; add no bypass. |
| Init does not select an impossible npm test | Preserve only parsed existing commands; template remains `{}` and setup reports CI-only rather than selecting npm. |
| Preflight precedes writers | Preserve `startIssue` preflight placement and test its static behavior; no process spawn is added. |
| Exact remediation | Add actionable config-path messages for all static failure classes. |
| Monorepo fixture | Extend `verification-preflight.test.ts` with root no-script and `web` script cases. |
| Required checks fail closed | Leave runtime verification/evaluation untouched and assert diagnostics/status contract remains blocking. |

### Out of Scope

- Automatic package discovery or arbitrary command synthesis.
- New verification schema versions or package-manager execution semantics.
- GitHub CI polling, PR creation, merge, issue closure, or cleanup.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History

- The frozen base already contains cwd normalization, static preflight, child-runtime cwd resolution, and a monorepo preflight fixture.
- The setup writer still assigns `verification.commands: {}` for every run, which is the remaining policy-integrity gap.

### Callers And Data Flow

- `loadForgePolicy` parses tracked `.forge/config.json` and normalizes command cwd.
- `configureForgePolicy` loads that policy, applies branch/CI/concurrency choices, serializes it, and currently drops local commands.
- `startIssue` prepares the frozen integration worktree, statically preflights required commands, then materializes agents and launches direct/orchestrated writers.
- `forge_verify` later resolves the bound cwd and executes only the tracked command name; merge evaluation treats missing/failed required reports as blocking.

### CI Surface

- Required named check: `check`, which runs `npm run check` from the repository root in this worktree.
- `npm test` covers the TypeScript test suite, including adapter/policy/UI regressions.
- `npm run typecheck` validates changed TypeScript and exported test helpers.
- GitHub CI remains parent-owned after PR preparation.

### Prior Findings

- Root package scripts may be absent while `web/package.json` defines `test`; static package-script inspection must not run npm.
- Existing cwd traversal/symlink/control-directory tests establish the safety baseline.

### Hazards

- Silently clearing tracked commands weakens the configured verification contract.
- A setup summary must not imply that CI-only verification is equivalent to local checks when commands are present.
- Diagnostics must preserve current testable substrings while adding remediation.
- Do not infer a package directory or synthesize a script from untrusted repository files.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add a small, side-effect-free init verification configuration/summary helper that deep-copies parsed command definitions, preserves their normalized cwd, and reports CI-only when the command map is empty.
2. Use that helper in `/forge:init` policy assembly and completion notification; keep template `{}` unchanged and optionally statically validate retained required commands before writing.
3. Strengthen `VerificationPreflightError` messages with the exact command policy path and concrete config or `/forge:init` remediation while retaining existing path prefixes and fail-closed checks.
4. Extend adapter tests for missing package directories, missing scripts, missing executables, and valid `web` cwd; extend UI tests for preservation versus CI-only summary behavior.
5. Update README only if the final setup behavior is not already documented, then run the bound `check` verification.

### Rollback Plan

Revert the single implementation commit; no external effects or schema migration are introduced.

### Risk Controls

- No subprocess invocation is added to preflight.
- Deep-copy command definitions prevents setup mutation from altering the loaded policy unexpectedly.
- Required commands remain present unless the tracked policy already has none.
- Existing runtime path checks and verification gate logic remain unchanged.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
